qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Patents and regulatory exclusivity on commercial therapies (Eliquis, Opdivo, Pomalyst, Yervoy, Reblozyl, Cobenfy) provide legal monopoly barriers during patent term. However, empirical proof of moat fails: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 8.2% and 5-year median is sub-10%, depressed by large goodwill and intangible additions from the $74B Celgene and $14B Karuna buyouts. Severe erosion threats include IRA price caps on Eliquis starting in 2026, followed by Eliquis LOE in 2028, Opdivo LOE in 2028, and generic cannibalization of Revlimid.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 8.2% < 12%, REJECT). 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 8.2% fails the 12% hurdle due to an invested capital base heavily inflated by the $74B Celgene and $14B Karuna acquisitions. BMY lacks enduring pricing power above inflation as its foundational blockbusters face severe patent cliff erosion and statutory price controls: Eliquis faces IRA Medicare price cuts in 2026 and generic entry in 2028, Opdivo loses exclusivity in 2028, and Revlimid suffers generic erosion. Backfilling these cliffs has trapped BMY on a capital-intensive M&A treadmill funded by $47B+ in debt.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC is 8.2%, below the 12% hurdle. 2024 GAAP net loss of $(8,948)M driven by $13,373M in acquired IPR&D charges from Karuna Therapeutics ($14B), RayzeBio, and Mirati acquisitions. Long-term debt reached $47.6B at FY2024. Core blockbusters Eliquis ($13B+ sales) and Opdivo ($9B+ sales) face imminent patent cliffs (Eliquis 2026-2028 LOE plus 2026 IRA price cuts; Opdivo 2028 LOE), demonstrating the lack of sustainable multi-cycle pricing power and structural reinvestment drag.
